prerequisites: It is highly recommended that the student has passed the subject Thermal Engineering, taught in the second year.
Mastery of Mechanics and Thermodynamics concepts taught in the first year.
Basic knowledge of Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Mathematical Methods taught in the first year is also convenient.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the fundamental energetic equations on which thermal machines are based.
Know the theoretical foundations on which spark ignition engines, compression ignition engines, steam turbines, and gas turbines are based.
Understand and solve questions related to spark ignition engines, compression ignition engines, steam turbines, and gas turbines.
Be able to analyze combined cycle plants.
Understand and solve questions related to cogeneration plants.

syllabus_topics: Generalities: classification of thermal machines. Energetic equations of thermal machines.
Fundamental characteristics of reciprocating internal combustion engines (ICE).
Fundamental parameters of ICE. Practical exercises.
Combustion in ICE. Fuel supply and ignition of Spark Ignition Engines (SIE). Fuel supply of Compression Ignition Engines (CIE).
teaching_methods: Virtual Campus activities (reading theoretical foundations, solving questionnaires, participating in discussion forums, viewing additional material)

assessment_methods.method: Submission of exercises proposed by the faculty, to be done by students outside the classroom (EV2)
Active student participation in the development of the subject through in-class exercises proposed by the faculty, solved and submitted by students during face-to-face sessions (EV4)

assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as (0.7 * EV1) + (0.1 * EV2) + (0.1 * EV3) + (0.1 * EV4). A minimum grade of 3.5 out of 10 is required for the in-person written exam (EV1). If this minimum is not met, the final grade will be the EV1 score. Grades for EV2, EV3, and EV4 are obtained during the course and are valid for all calls of the academic year.
